name: South Sudan
headline: South Sudan: +41.4% growth in 2025, 97.6% inflation, debt 64% of GDP
sections: South Sudan is a $5.5 billion economy (2025), the world's 171st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +41.4% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%.

Consumer prices rose 97.6% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, up from −3.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 12.4% (2023), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 18.5% (2023).
Gross government debt is 64% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 48% in 2020. The general government balance is +3.3% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is −6.4% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need.
IMF projections put government debt at 46% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 57.7 years (2024). Population: 12.2 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
